page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.4xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors running at a baseline frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 4.0 GB memory-per-core ratio.

A defining characteristic of this instance is its bundled local storage, which consists of 47,244 GB of Hard Disk Drive (HDD) capacity. This massive local storage volume is paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. No graphics processing units (GPUs) are included in this configuration.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.d1.4xlarge offers a high volume of local HDD storage relative to its compute and memory allocation, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring massive capacity without the premium cost of solid-state drives (SSDs). However, the reliance on traditional HDD technology presents a performance tradeoff, as sequential and random input/output operations per second (IOPS) will be significantly lower than SSD-backed alternatives. Additionally, the Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 represents an older CPU generation, which lacks newer instruction sets such as AVX-512.

This hardware profile is engineered for workloads that demand substantial storage capacity and sequential data access rather than high-speed random IOPS. Suitable use cases include large-scale data warehousing, MapReduce jobs, distributed file systems like HDFS, log processing, and cold data archiving.
